chunks: Humayd, from Ibn Sama'a, from Ibn Rabat, from Ays ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a man who gave his wife the choice (khul'), so she chose herself [to be divorced], and she was irrevocably divorced from him.
He said: No, this is something that was specific to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He was commanded with that, so he did it.
And if they had chosen themselves, he would have divorced them.
And this is the Word of Allah, Exalted and Majestic: 'Say to your wives: If you desire the life of this world and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and let you go with a good release.'

key_terms.خَيَّرَ: gave the choice (referring to the specific right of the Prophet's wives to choose between staying or divorcing)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the Prophet's 'choice' (khul') and the general Islamic ruling for divorce?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that the specific mechanism of 'choice' (Takhayyur) where the Prophet's wives could initiate separation was a unique divine privilege (Khassiyyah) granted exclusively to them, distinct from the general ruling of Khul' applicable to other Muslims. This exclusivity is rooted in Surah Al-Ahzab (33:28-29), where Allah commanded the Prophet to offer his wives this choice, and the Imam notes that if they had chosen separation, he would have divorced them, confirming the verse's direct application to their specific status.
